item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: The Architects Automaton
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the feedback.

Spoiler below

+ show block
– hide block

The reason why It's vague is that it is a mystery note that develops over time. I have to decide between balancing what to say here and what not to spoil in what is effectively the general outline of the story. The problem is that anyone who is actually interested in the concept enough to greenlight it would also end up being spoiled to the story in the long run. I explained in my spoiler post for Cyber exactly why it has the effects it has. It is definitely not just a simple "it drives people insane", but the exact specifics of what it is doing and why it is doing it can fill out 400 words all on it's own and is a huge part of unraveling the mystery that I don't just want to spoil for readers.

In which care, should I care about that at all and just spill everything out?

My ultimate point is already written out as it pertains to the SPC's themselves.
But spoilers kill a story, so I'm not really sure what to do here.
And in my honest opinion, as it pertains to the mystery, I have already said too much in an effort to get greenlit for a sandbox that can't be justified in merely 400 words, but rather should be justified by the reading of the draft article itself.

is the real problem for a story… I would suggest thinking of some other effect seeing the patterns does…

Not a problem at all, because its effects are not random in the slightest and it is not merely just "driving someone insane". The idea here is that everything psychological that seems to be random is actually simply the extreme of things that already exist in the subjects, even in tiny quantities. The idea here is to put on a display that everyone, EVERYONE has some tiny piece of their mind that is not quite right, no matter how small. These patterns have hidden within them traps that latch on and exploit these small problems and cause them to grow to extremes, all in an effort to protect its creator's knowledge. Basically, the machine's patterns are not driving you insane or causing devastating mental diseases, they are simply magnifying the issues that are already there. The idea is that everyone, EVERYONE has some mental issue somewhere, no matter how small they may be. If that's not different enough of a tone then I don't really know what to say there. I'll take it back to the drawing board.

why make people crazy? What else could be done to make it unsettling?

I noted that in the spoiler for Cyber, but that is really the question here. WHY is it doing what it is doing? And the answer is written, but hidden from view because that answer literally answers the mystery of the entire object. I'll probably rewrite or update the greenlight with some spoiler sections explaining the actual story at hand, so that people can read and avoid the context should they care to read along once the story is actually unfolding as an SCP, interviews and experiment logs.

item.title: Re: New SCiP: Just A Very Common Spectroscope (awaiting greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

As the energy carried by light will magnify with the shortening of wave length, energy coming from nowhere accumulates in the universe and finally caused… deviation of balance of material and energy. Then unexpected results, like the worst - affect the gradual cosmic expansion or bring near the final collapse.

This feels…like a lot of escalation? Like I get why there's ever growing amounts of energy in the system cos the effects of this changing the wavelength and increasing the energy of light; but it feels…like the universe is so large that this effect would be drowned out by the sheer size of the universe long before it became an actual issue; particularly since you can e.g. put it deep underground with minimal light in the style of a Neutrino Detector.

Even ignoring this, how are you showing this escalation within the article? What do you like, intend to do to convey the threat and have folk try to like, prevent it happening and like, actually get a reader invested in this escalation?

The name 'spectroscope' is probably fine; it's very much the kinda thing you're going to have to describe by like, explaining what it does regardless of name so *shrugs*

Not very sure how to merge the final world-threatening narrative into this ordinary object-describing document. Will a research report (regarding the status of the universe) or a test log work well?

This question raises a lot of concern in me. See, the answer very much depends on what the actual world-threatening narrative is and how you want to tell it: perhaps a series of updates over thousands of years would work if it's slow (see e.g. SCP-4792 for an example of this kind of thing), or some journal entries from a researcher attached to it if you want a quick thing, or some mix of the two. But at it's core, it really just depends on how the story like…unfolds?

item.title: A way to die. (SCP/ Tales idea)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (Maybe a tale too? *More in Additional Notes)

Genre (Optional): Action, Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout with quite some addendums (incident report + psychological report + phone call + several Interviews + operational execution Protocol + some more)

Elevator Pitch: My article will tell a story about the SCP Foundation and an SCP struggling to find common ground. SCP-XXXX wants to die, but cant. The Foundation wants to contain it, but is not able to do so. A researcher wants to mediate between these two parties, and pays dearly for the attempt. And with the conflict ongoing, more and more people are being drawn into it.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, one protagonist in the story, has an seemingly simple ability. When dead, its consciousness is transferred in to another body. By that method it is profiting from the knowledge and life experience of every man it has ever bin. Yet it wants to die one last time, tired of the endless life it was gifted, and realises that despite being nearly omniscient, the SCP cant figure out how. In despair it turns to the SCP Foundation that made the fatal error to underrate the SCPs power.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Straightaway it is clear, the SCP Foundation fears SCP-XXXX. But the SCP seems to be completely harmless at its first appearances in the documents. A closer look however reveals, that not its ability is hazardous, but the sheer amount of knowledge it owns about not only science, psychology or self defence, but about the SCP Foundation. Threatened, the Foundation by reflex draws its sword, forgetting that what they attempt to fight is immortal.

Additional Notes: *I, unwisely, already have started a draft without waiting for an reply by qualified reviewers. But when I paused tipping, I noticed that the word counter was already indicating 3000 words (I am not even finished jet), of which only 600 are taken up by the actual SCP document. So I am not only looking for an GREENLIGHT here, but also seek for an experts opinion. Is it just a very long SCP, or would it be better to make it a SCP with an associated Tale. Feel free to ask me for the draft if needed. I do even recommend it for reading, if you need to get a clearer picture of what I tried to sum up in 399 words here.

I love this SCP, and like all DoMc SCPs I'm unable to adequately explain any of it. The short compositions are a lot of fun too. Strong +1.

Small nitpick: in the description, it said the melody doesn't fit into any popularly known scale. This isn't correct because it fits into the 12-tone or chromatic scale (unless there's something going on with microtonal variation that's not transcribed). It would be more accurate to say it doesn't reflect any common diatonic scale.

Overall, the melody isn't unusual, it's actually pretty simple and really pleasant, which adds to the mystery I think. I tried to deal music analysis, but no description fits neatly. It's simply C major with some chromatic variation. Overall, well done.

It's awesome to see you want to contribute to the site - I really can't wait to see what you'll come up with. If you're going to try your hands at writing for the site seriously though, you'll want to click that little red collapsible at the bottom of this comment - there, you'll find a plethora of useful resources created for the purpose of guiding new members of the site towards guides and other resources which will definitely help you improve your writing and seek help on it.

Without further ado though, let's actually click it, shall we? :)

+ show block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: any suggestions for my SCP?
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I'm not really a fan of the central narrative section; it feels…too expected and too focussed on the backstory of this. My general advice when writing a SCP is to forget about why it exists (and how the Foundation found it, a little). In general, backstory is not the most interesting angle because it happens a) before the foundation get involved (and so, before any of the PoV characters can be there) and b) it's just, not very interesting; and this suffers from this a lot since there's not really any way for the Foundation to know about the mans' gradual discovery of his powers, not a lot happens while he discovers them, and it's very temporally removed from the here and now and the people involved in the story.

Like, at the end of the day, you're trying to write an interesting short story about a weird thing, not an actual technical report on it; and so you really have to figure out why the weird thing existing is interesting and how it's existence affects the Foundation: like, do they use this man as like, a living transcriber? Do they run experiments on him? Does his ability pose difficulties because of some unforeseen aspect of them?

Part of my concern here is that the effects of the man are very…straightforward? One of the really hard parts of writing a scp is balancing the anomalous properties so that they're complex enough that you can do something interesting to explore what they mean whilst also not creating a big, overcomplex mess of properties that's hard for a reader to understand whilst also not being interesting. The Journey of Your First SCP: Part I talks about this a lot when it discusses 'depth vs complexity': at the moment, your anomaly is neither complex nor deep, and so there's not a lot of interesting things that it like…leads to a person being able to do; and I think this is why you're struggling a little to find the interesting thing here.

My suggestion would be to consider the emotions here: like, maybe there's an interesting angle where you can explore the effect that being in containment has on the man, and how it makes 'em feel; or perhaps you can figure out a reason for him to be in some like, really severe containment and so in turn, make a reader feel empathically sad at the Foundations treatment of him, or something.

It might be worth having a read of e.g. An exercise in narrative based SCPs and How Not to Walk Your Dog: An Essay on Pacing to really get a feel for like, how to do something interesting with the SCP idea.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
We talked a bit in IRC for crit on the first two iterations. The third one is going to be a bit more in-depth.

Line by line
That's just fine

SCP-XXXX is presumably made from an alloy of palladium and black rhodium. The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability of acquiring a sample.

This can be one sentence: Although it cannot be confirmed due to the difficulty of acquiring a sample, SCP-XXXX is presumably made from an alloy of palladium and black rhodium.

SCP-XXXX is the object that the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

This seems out of place here, I'd recommend either omitting it (since that's what you imply with the von Zeppelin stuff later) or putting it with the von Zeppelin stuff. It just doesn't seem related to anything else being discussed in this section.

SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity whose age nor origin have been successfully investigated. It claims that these are untraceable because it is a being that was spontaneously formed in the universe.

This is a big deal with part of the reason behind the importance of clinical tone: The Foundation wants to do their best to keep people from getting emotionally attached to anomalies and related beings, so calling it by its preferred name here is a big no-no. I'd recommend this:

"SCP-XXXX-1 is a sapient entity of currently unknown age and origin. During communication with the entity, it has claimed that these details are unknown even to itself, as it was spontaneously formed in the universe."

SCP-XXXX-1 travels through space in search of dying stars. Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will collect the star and store it inside SCP-XXXX. SCP-XXXX-1 has been observed leaping several lightyears worth of distance by Beholder-3. It hasn't elaborated on its way of traveling nor how it can interact with stars. Its whereabouts are currently unknown.

This whole paragraph is a bit haphazardly constructed, and has some issues with tone as well. I'd go with something along the lines of:

"The propulsion method employed by SCP-XXXX is currently unknown. It has been observed by the Beholder-3 satellite to travel several light years nigh instantaneously, and is nearly impossible to track because of this. SCP-XXXX-1 utilizes SCP-XXXX to travel through space in search of dying stars. Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will collect the star and store it inside SCP-XXXX. The entity has not explained the method of propulsion or the mechanism by which it interacts with stars."

Discovery: On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen SCP-XXXX with his telescope. He was administered amnestics, however due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

We discussed this section while talking about its iteration on a previous page, the same comments apply here.

Over the years, von Zeppelin showed more interest in air-travel. After internal discussion, the Foundation decided to allow von Zeppelin to invent new aircraft with undercover personnel beside him as manual laborers. It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX. Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin is the most accurate representation.

A few more issues with tone and structure here.

"Presumably due to the remnants of the memory of SCP-XXXX, von Zeppelin developed a vested interest in air travel. After internal discussion, Foundation administrative staff decided to allow von Zeppelin to create new aircraft with undercover Foundation personnel acting as manual laborers in his employ. It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop an aircraft based on the design of SCP-XXXX. Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin is the most accurate representation, though it is significantly smaller in size."

On 28 August 1903, several researchers observed SCP-XXXX near the Orion Arm and confirmed that this was the same object von Zeppelin saw 30 years ago by its description.

We discussed this section on IRC as well.

On 25 February 1955, the Foundation successfully launched the probes from "The Beholder Line" in space for further research of the universe. On 29 July 1958, SCP-XXXX was observed by Beholder-3 nearly 55 years after its last observation.

I think the quotes around The Beholder Line are unneeded, and it should probably read as 'the Beholder series'. We know the dates involved and can see it was nearly 55 years, so that part is unnecessary.

On 2 July 1962, "The Diplomat", a new probe was launched in space towards Beholder-3 to establish a direct way of communication and give the following objects to the passengers of SCP-XXXX:

  • Several syllabi and audio files of 57 languages.
  • Photographs of life on Earth, and music approved by several site-directors.
  • A transmitter, a receiver, and other equipment

A few minor formatting and tone fixes:

On 2 July 1962, the Diplomat probe was launched in the direction of Beholder-3 with the purpose of establishing a direct line of communication with SCP-XXXX, as well as delivering the following to the passenger(s):

  • Audio files of 57 different Earth languages.
  • Photographs of life on Earth, and music approved by several site directors. (What music?)
  • A transmitter, a receiver, and other equipment

The plural of syllable is syllables, not syllabi. Unless you meant, like, school lesson syllabi, which would be a bit odd since we don't even know if the thing knows our language at all. And why 57 languages specifically? You may want to look into the details of what NASA sent on the gold records put in the Voyager satellites. And what "other equipment" was included? Being so specific in certain regards leads to questions when things like this are left vague. Perhaps just "deep-space radio communication equipment"?

On 14 August 1986, SCP-XXXX-1 answered.

Slight tonal change:

" On 14 August 1986, a response from SCP-XXXX-1 was recorded."

14/08/1986 SCP-XXXX-1:
ARE YOU THERE? BIST DU DA? ÊTES-VOUS LA?

| OTHER LANGUAGES OMITTED FOR BREVITY

Why have three languages displayed, but others omitted? How many languages did it reply with in total? All 57?

Due to the distance and interference, it took each message one week to travel the distance between both parties, full communication logs available below.

More slight tonal changes:

"Due to the distance and interference inherent in deep space radio communication technology, each message took approximately seven days to fully transmit. Full communication logs are available below."

The whole communication log:

This part is definitely an awkward read. I don't know that I want to break it all down individually, but let me lay out a few problems:

  • Something that barely understands our language is giving itself names like The Star Euthanizer and The Pilgrim Between The Suns? Those are not exactly low-level linguistics. Reading on, I can see that it has clearly learned English before, but nobody in the Foundation seems to pick up on this, when at this point in their communication, as far as they know, this is the first time a human has communicated with it. They're not suspicious of this at all?
  • You mention earlier in the article that details like how the ship's propulsion system works are unknown, but nobody seems to be asking anything about the ship here. I'd think that in the 80s, the Foundation would be pretty damn interested in figuring out the mechanics of FTL travel.
  • Why Glen? Is there any significance to that name? Why not send it a list of common Earth names and let it choose one?
  • The Foundation half of the communication feels very informal at times considering that this would presumably be a really big deal. For example: "YOU KNOW THAT DYING STARS ARE HIGHLY EXPLOSIVE, RIGHT?" ", right?" is really informal. "WE DON'T KNOW A LOT ABOUT YOU " should be something like "WE HAVE LITTLE INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR STATUS OR HISTORY". "THEN WHAT AFTER YOU COLLECTED THE LAST ONE?" is another example. These are highly trained, educated, intelligent scientists communicating with an extraterrestrial in deep space, not a few friends catching up over coffee.
  • "I AM THE OLDEST VACUUMBORN BY FAR" he's so old that the concept of time itself is lost to him, but he knows he's the oldest one out there? That seems odd.
  • Him changing his title at the end of every message seems really unnecessary and is just sort of distracting throughout the logs. Didn't he ask to be given a name so that titles and labels wouldn't be used?
  • Why does something as old as time care about wishing humans a happy new year?
  • "YOU HAVE ALWAYS GIVEN ME THE SAME NAME." This thing has reset the universe god knows how many times, but whoever communicates with it always gives it the same name? That's a hell of a coincidence, don't you think?

By an 11:2 vote, it is accepted that SCP-XXXX-1 is responsible for a ZK Universe Reset Scenario but does not directly pose a threat to humanity.

All we have at this point is this thing's word. Even with the technology for FTL travel and containing a star before it goes supernova, there doesn't appear to be any actual evidence that it has the ability to reset the universe. If this was accepted by a vote, I'd think it'd be a much closer ratio than 11:2.

And at the end of it all, why would they not want to contain something with the power to reset the universe? How is that "not directly posing a threat to humanity"??? It may not be attacking us, but resetting the universe is literally the end of the world as we know it. That's not a threat?

The overall idea here is solid, but honestly the article really starts to break down a bit once you get to the communication logs. There's just so much that the Foundation is willing to take at face value when the only solid information they have is pretty limited. There are a myriad of ways it could learn things like the term O5 that don't involve having communicated with the Foundation in a past iteration of the universe, and they just accept that too easily for me to swallow. Unfortunately, I'm not really certain how you'd go about fixing this. I also didn't get much of any emotional response from it, it was more of just an "oh, that's what it's doing." The fact that the spacecraft was the inspiration for the design of the Zeppelin is given great prominence in the earlier iterations, but it seems to end up not really meaning anything besides a one-off line in the communication logs. This is an entity that claims to be as old as time itself and was willed into existence by the universe, and I seem to be more curious about it than the Foundation are.

I guess the best way I can wrap it up is to say that I feel like there's not that much of a narrative here - it's just a list of things happening and a conversation. There wasn't much that made me want to keep reading other than the Zeppelin stuff, and again, that didn't really seem to end up meaning anything.

item.title: Re: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Gonna be honest: I don't really vibe with this. It feels…like a kinda stereotypical 'descent into madness' kinda story without really doing much to like, distinguish itself? Like it feels reminiscent of something like SCP-3000 or SCP-4391 but in a much more restrained way than the second and without the narrative heft of the first. In some ways, the uncertainty of the description of the SCP feels reminiscent of stuff like SCP-252 or a lot of antimemetic related stuff.

Beyond this, the way the narrative plays out feels…iunno, I think having it be framed as transcripts from the last surviving agent will really kill all the tension because we'll immediately know that everything the people do to try to survive will be futile and so it might be really hard to capture a readers interest. You might be able to manage a kinda, deep dread here where like, because we know it's futile, we just, are faced with the inevitability of the end; but it feels like that'd be really hard to do well.

On a very minor note, I have no idea how 'Midnight Sun' ties in here as a name.

Normally I'd offer some advice on how to improve this but I just, generally think it's not hugely something that appeals to me so you might find other reviewers are more receptive to it; or you might find that like, really leaning into the weirdness with it more, or like, doing more with it than just 'everyone ends up dying' would help?

You wouldn't necessarily have to change a lot of the plot beats for this; including the presence of the Foundation, but it'd allow you to really focus on the important stuff and also to not worry about how to answer the question of 'how does anyone know what happened here'.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How does the Foundation contain an anomaly when 1) it's both multiplying itself out of control 2) it blends in very well with non-anomalous common animals and 3) the effect it grants is potentially beneficial to ordinary citizens who would seek out out.

item.content:encoded:
The idea came to me watching a hypercube building block demonstration. […] I imagined how a 4+ dimensional entity would appear to us […] This inter-dimensional nature of the beast is the whole point.

I don't see any of that reflected in the current concept presented. If you want to focus on the wonders of thinking in more than 3 dimensions, don't have the core anomaly focused on the terrible things it does.

+ show block
– hide block

As I understand it D-Class are recruited from death row inmates. Someone convicted of a sadistic murder should be at the top of their list. Additionally, from my reading, D-Class are directly exposed to anomalies all the time

The issue here is that you're assuming that the in-universe Foundation would conveniently happen to recruit this anomaly as a D-Class, and conveniently test it enough to expose it to multiple anomalies. As a reader, I find the entire setup questionable, since not only is it odd that the Foundation thought that this "sadistic murderer" person was someone they could just lump in with all the other D-Class, they also trusted them enough to expose them to multiple anomalies, rather than one or two. Granted, some readers may suspend their disbelief enough to not be too bothered by this setup, but combined with all the other plot contrivances the storyline for me seems more authorial meddling than believably developing narrative.

It's triggered on purpose by the Anomalous-D while being tasked with routine maintenance. An example might be purposefully breaking eye-contact with SCP-173 while cleaning its cell in order to feed off the trauma of either the creature or the other D-Class in the room

Again, if the dude is a sadistic murderer with no sense of self-preservation or empathy, why is the Foundation trusting them with anything? If they really want to use the guy as a lab rat, it would be for protocols with the absolute simplest instructions and plenty of safeguards in case the guy goes rogue. For this case I personally feel like an in-universe researcher would deem the guy not worth the trouble to test on (unless the nature of the anomaly necessitates a test subject who is almost ludicrously volatile and dangerous).

But they have. The SCP-682-E addendum recounts exactly this. And it makes perfect sense. There are at least two entities that I can think of that are on a termination list and the Foundation doesn't know how they're going to kill them.

SCP-682 was written almost a decade ago and is one dangerous anomaly out of thousands. Most readers aren't going to take your premise seriously if you need to rely on super-old (and frankly, not great examples of current site standards) Series I articles to support your reasoning for the Foundation acting irrationally.

I'm also playing with the notion that our thoughts, souls and emotions do exist on planes that we don't have conscious access to. Yet our emotions and souls are tied to our bodies, and in that way we are all extra-dimensional beings.

You might want to consider a tale or GoI format entry then, since the level of non-observable knowledge required to understand this thing empirically seems to necessitate omnipresence that the in-universe Foundation wouldn't have.

I've highlighted its potential because I'm thinking of the stories that follow next. If this entity is to live in isolation it will be just like so many others. It will be just another mystery in a box that says nothing about the larger world and how things work together. To me that is uninteresting.

If the core article is downvoted to deletion range, it doesn't matter how many stories beyond the first page you've planned. Focus on making the SCP entity enjoyable to read as a standalone first, and then if the audience response to it is good then you can start think about branching out. If you try too hard to force openings for additional followup works, it'll just feel contrived and overreaching.

In general though, I feel like your plans for the page are way more complicated and large-scale than I personally would enjoy reading about. At this point I think your best bet is to reach out to authors of high-rated extradimensional SCP articles (you can find them with the Tag Search) and see what they think of what you have planned.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: “Patient Zero”
item.content:encoded:
Hey there eNCiVi, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither an official reviewer (but I am a flight officer) nor a hugely experienced one, so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
- Close Section-by-Section -

Elevator Pitch

So my main problem with this pitch is in two parts: it is quite overpowered (OP) and it is a humanoid (not a problem in itself, but I'll explain further along).
OP anomalies break the suspension of disbelief of readers if not executed correctly, and said execution is hard to do. Without this execution, OP anomalies feel slightly ridiculous and unrealistic, a surefire way to get downvotes on your article.
Humanoids are one of the hardest types of anomaly to write. Similarly to OP anomalies, they require great execution to not become downvote magnets. Without proper execution, they don't fit with the tone of the Site and feel more like a comic-book character rather than an SCP.

Central Narrative

There isn't very much here in regards to narrative. All you have is some testing logs and a vague incident which you fail to elaborate on because it is TBD1. This may have been acceptable in Series I, but people expect more in Series VI. Find an emotion you want the readers to feel, and use it to build up your narrative.

Hook/Attention Grabber

This is frustratingly vague and nothing more. Don't keep up the 'mystery' of your concept and try to keep it secret after posting in the forums, explain it! Tell us what the mystery is and what's behind it, otherwise it just makes it harder to critique your idea.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I'm quite doubtful about this

To put it bluntly, your anomaly is an OP humanoid which has little to no story behind it besides a vague 'incident' which isn't elaborated on. Not only this, but it is strange to me that it is only immune to the abilities of some of the most dangerous SCPs. Why? I am also getting slight self-insert 'vibes' (for lack of a better word that comes to mind) from this concept, which isn't good. I'd recommend it four things:

1. Consider reworking your concept. As it stands, it's quite OP and contrived.
2. Rework your narrative. Elaborate! Make me feel something!
3. Check out the Guide Hub for advice and essays on how to do the above two points. It's a great resource!
4. Contact some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad, they have tonnes of experience and are able to provide some great crit!


Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
Footnotes
1. Always finish off your idea before posting it in the forums, otherwise it makes it more difficult for us critters to critique it.

item.title: The Empathy Infection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama

Page Layout: Standard containment procedures, description, discovery, testing logs and containment report.

Elevator Pitch: A sculpture of "The Three Graces" that spreads an memetic infection of emotional empathy. It was commissioned from an anartist for the Manna Charitable Foundation as an attempt to increase charitable acts. In particular, acts that include helping people normally considered of a lower class or importance. This extends to trying to protect these individuals from harm.

Any close viewing of charitable acts caused by the infection further spreads it to the viewer. The effect can also be spread through images and videos. This allows online spread of the memetic effect though literal viral posts and stories.

Central Narrative: Sites near [liberal city] experiences difficulty treating D-class as disposable and accepting collateral loss of life. An investigation looks into the situation and also finds increased charity efforts and the near elimination of homelessness in a large portion of the country. Further investigation discovers the infection. Originating from the sculpture newly installed in the city's downtown area.

The foundation confiscates the statue and tests antimemes for internal use. The site regains the ability to find D-Class suffering and death acceptable via the antimemetics. Using online bots they deploy these antimemes within disparaging and skeptical comments on the viral posts. Nearly all posts are effected and debased as either attention seeking or faked. This extents into offline instances being 'inoculated' by onlookers heckling and mocking the charitable acts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Exploring the idea that the foundation works beyond compassion. Thus cannot exist in a world that is dedicated to it.

Additional Notes: I'm playing with the idea that the foundation is worried the viral posts could become resistant. Thus they are forced to worry not if they are too immoral, but too moral in their acts.

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for this review. You've put a lot of work into it and I appreciate that. Having said that, I am left wondering if the content is actually this bad or if i've just failed to convey what I'm trying to do.

The idea came to me watching a hypercube building block demonstration. You can see it here.

I imagined how a 4+ dimensional entity would appear to us if some part of it were to intersect with our 3 D reality. I think we would perceive it as an anomaly.

In the story I'm trying to construct, a creature like SCP 682 is potentially vast – existing simultaneously across multiple dimensions. SCP researchers are vainly trying to terminate the thing by finding novel ways to blast the small fraction of it that they’ve snared in our reality.

I'm inspired to work along these lines because I'm interested in root causes. The SCP universe is now populated by something like 5000 anomalies with little sense of coherent rhyme. I'm excited by the opportunity to contribute to cannon in a way that suggests an inter-relationship between phenomena. Make some of them make a little more sense.

+ show block
– hide block

don't make this thing an interdimensional traveler.

This inter-dimensional nature of the beast is the whole point. Its existence across dimensions is what gives me the opportunity to play with interconnection between anomalies along planes that we humans don't have access to.

don't have the Foundation recruit it as a D-Class.

As I understand it D-Class are recruited from death row inmates. A drifter with no family who's been convicted of a sadistic murder should be at the top of their list. Additionally, from my reading, D-Class are directly exposed to anomalies all the time

don't have there be a random breach that randomly involves the entity.

The breach would not be random. It's triggered on purpose by the Anomalous-D while being tasked with routine maintenance. An example might be purposefully breaking eye-contact with SCP-173 while cleaning its cell in order to feed off the trauma of either the creature or the other D-Class in the room

the Foundation has contained tons of dangerous anomalies that could injure or destroy other anomalies, but they're not clamoring to use those either

But they have. The SCP-682-E addendum recounts exactly this. And it makes perfect sense. There are at least two entities that I can think of that are on a termination list and the Foundation doesn't know how they're going to kill them.

give it more emotional/intellectual depth than "does terrible things, makes people feel bad, because that's what it was conceptualized to do". Does it have any self-awareness of what has to do to survive? Does it have any redeeming qualities as an individual? This would be the main spot to flesh out, since generic danger effects are pretty common, and often seen in low-rated and deleted works.

Admittedly my thoughts here are less complete. But what I'm working with is the idea that it's a chameleon which takes on the shapes of the reality that it inhabits. It has no emotions and it's not truly sapient. It functions like an extremely sophisticated chatbot mimicking the patterns around it (I am aware of the problems of squaring that with its passing as a D-Class human for weeks).

It stays in one reality only as long as it can feed and then it drifts into another.

I'm also playing with the notion that our thoughts, souls and emotions do exist on planes that we don't have conscious access to. Yet our emotions and souls are tied to our bodies, and in that way we are all extra-dimensional beings. Anomalous-D feeds on the part of us (of all things) that's not corporal. It is able to heighten our emotional states by torturing our corporal bodies. Like squeezing juice from a fruit.

remove the unusually insistent focus on this thing's "potential" usefulness.

I've highlighted its potential because I'm thinking of the stories that follow next. If this entity is to live in isolation it will be just like so many others. It will be just another mystery in a box that says nothing about the larger world and how things work together. To me that is uninteresting.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: SCP Idea SEEKING GREENLIGHT
item.content:encoded:
Page type: New SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: This SCP would be something simple, something that makes you wonder "How can a Hot-air balloon do this?"
Central Narrative: ISo my SCP is a man in a hot air balloon that is designated safe as he only attacks in self defense. The Hot-Air balloon itself can reach up to extremely fast speeds and stop on a time and do things such as move in any direction or things like barrel rolls. A real physics breaking type entity. For example, the Balloon can easily reach Mach 3 and then stop instantly with no inertia, no drag, nothing and the man in said balloon doesn't fly out of the balloon or do any type of bracing for the oncoming stop. The SCP itself can initiate maneuvers such as barrel rolls.
Hook: The hook is that it has that funny/weird feel to it while not being that ridiculous that it takes people of out it.
From what I read I have to get the concept greenlight then the draft and then the final green light for it to become and "Canon" article.
Additional: I'm just thinking of how to "Fill" more of so It's not just a few paragraphs.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Merit to Match
item.content:encoded:
I have mixed feelings about this one.
On one hand it does have an interesting spin on the self help genre, on the other it expresses a biased and harmful idea of justice and merit. The examples you gave made me cringe, being rich isn't a virtue and being poor isn't a character flaw. I suppose you gave these examples off the top of your head but if you take this forward I strongly recommend changing this. As it is this PoI isn't making much of a change in the world, they are just endorsing the current system and by the tone of their threat I feel like they want to shake things up.
